name: United Utilities wastewater pre-development
fact: United Utilities uses pre-development enquiry to agree drainage strategy, points of connection and discharge rates and to identify potential drainage problems early.
gate: Pre-development advice is not a formal sewer connection, planning consent or permanent capacity reservation.

name: United Utilities wastewater pre-development enquiry form
fact: The current form requests site address, grid reference, units, site area, planning status, phasing and proposed drainage information; the service aims to respond within 15 working days.
gate: Submission and response timing do not equal technical approval or sewer capacity guarantee.

name: United Utilities wastewater planning
fact: The company advises developers to review network maps and use pre-development guidance before starting works, including sustainable drainage and asset-protection considerations.
gate: Network-map discovery is not exact surveyed asset position or capacity confirmation.

name: United Utilities sewer adoption
fact: The adoption process begins with pre-planning to agree drainage strategy, connection points and discharge rates before design and legal adoption stages.
gate: S104 adoption workflow is separate from planning permission and network-capacity evidence.

name: United Utilities S104 sewer adoption application
fact: The S104 application requests planning reference, drainage plan, hydraulic calculations, SuDS details, ground conditions and land-registry-compliant plans.
gate: An application package does not mean technical acceptance, legal adoption or planning approval.

name: United Utilities developer levels of service
fact: United Utilities publishes developer-service targets including pre-planning acknowledgement and full-response times for sewerage enquiries.
gate: Service-level compliance is not evidence of site capacity or connection rights.

name: United Utilities developer document library
fact: The current library separates pre-development, water connections, sewer requisitions, diversions, adoptions, build-over and technical guidance documents.
gate: Availability of guidance documents does not establish approval for a target development.

name: United Utilities application forms and guidance
fact: The application index routes developer customers to pre-development, wastewater, water, self-lay and NAV processes.
gate: Correct form selection is procedural and not a technical or planning decision.

name: Anglian Water planning and capacity
fact: Anglian Water's pre-planning service performs desktop assessment of water and foul/surface drainage needs and can identify connection points, alternatives and potential network upgrades.
gate: Desktop assessment is not final design, legal connection approval or permanent headroom reservation.

name: Anglian Water planning and capacity application routes
fact: 2026-27 services distinguish modelled water reports, foul feasibility/detailed assessments, surface-water assessments and optional additional modelling/site surveys.
gate: A paid modelled report remains evidence for feasibility, not a guarantee that later planning or capacity evidence will remain unchanged.

name: Anglian Water surface water risk management
fact: Anglian Water requires developers to consider surface-water disposal hierarchy and risk before seeking a surface-water connection to its network.
gate: Surface-water connection preference or assessment does not replace LPA/LLFA drainage approval.

name: Anglian Water 2026-27 development services charging arrangements
fact: The 2026-27 schedule distinguishes non-domestic capacity, modelled water pre-planning, foul Tier 1/Tier 2, surface-water and additional modelling services.
gate: A charging schedule defines service scope and price, not outcome or available capacity.

name: Yorkshire Water water pre-planning enquiry
fact: Yorkshire Water provides a desktop pre-planning report on network availability, restrictions and capacity; the page states information is subject to final review and confirmation at later stages.
gate: A positive pre-planning report is not a final connection offer or reserved capacity.

name: Yorkshire Water sewerage pre-planning enquiry
fact: Yorkshire Water checks whether the public sewer can accept proposed foul/surface flows and suggests connection points or possible studies/upgrades where capacity is insufficient.
gate: Desktop views and suggested points are not hydraulic design approval or planning consent.

name: Yorkshire Water developer sewerage services
fact: Developer services include pre-planning, sewer connections, adoptions, diversions, capital-scheme support and asset checks.
gate: Service availability is not evidence of a site's remaining network headroom.

name: Wessex Water developer services
fact: Wessex Water separates planning/capacity, network maps, water, wastewater, nutrient-neutrality and DWMP resources for development.
gate: A service catalogue is not a site-specific capacity or consent result.

name: Wessex Water planning and capacity
fact: Wessex Water recommends early engagement before planning and offers capacity/location advice, pre-planning enquiry and standing guidance.
gate: Early capacity advice does not itself reserve capacity or approve drainage design.

name: Wessex Water network maps
fact: Wessex Water provides water-main and sewer plans but explicitly advises exact asset position should be surveyed before intrusive work and private drains may not be shown.
gate: Map linework is not exact surveyed asset geometry and cannot alone establish buildability.

name: Wessex Water new water mains
fact: For large multi-unit development, Wessex Water recommends pre-development capacity/location enquiry and requires planning approval before a new-main application.
gate: Planning approval and water-main delivery are separate gates; neither implies the other.

name: Wessex Water sewer connection
fact: A new sewer connection requires Wessex Water consent; pumped rising mains need additional septicity information and technical controls.
gate: A capacity indication is not sewer-connection consent.

name: Wessex Water self-lay
fact: Accredited WIRS self-lay providers can install new water mains/services and Wessex Water can later adopt compliant networks.
gate: Self-lay route changes delivery mechanics, not water-capacity or planning status.

name: Wessex Water single dwelling connections
fact: New sewer or water connections require Wessex Water consent and use separate application/guidance processes.
gate: Planning approval does not equal water/sewer connection consent.

name: Wessex Water nutrient neutral development position
fact: The position statement addresses nutrient-neutral development in sensitive catchments and notes private treatment arrangements can require LPA, Natural England and Environment Agency approval.
gate: Wastewater treatment option or WRC context does not itself satisfy nutrient-neutrality or planning requirements.

name: Southern Water pre-planning enquiries
fact: Southern Water's optional pre-planning enquiry provides an early water/wastewater capacity view, connection point assessment and asset-crossing flags; the response is not approval/refusal and is valid for 12 months.
gate: A pre-planning response is time-limited information, not design approval or planning consent.

name: Southern Water sewer connection
fact: A public sewer connection requires Southern Water approval; larger development should check capacity through wastewater pre-planning first.
gate: Planning permission does not authorize an unapproved public sewer connection.

name: Southern Water sewer requisitions
fact: Where a site lacks practical sewer access, developers may request a Section 98 sewer requisition with drainage/easement and route information.
gate: Requisition availability does not prove a feasible final route, land rights or delivery timetable.

name: Southern Water technical handbooks and documents
fact: The current library includes surface-water management, SuDS, source-protection-zone, sewer connection, adoption and water-connection guidance.
gate: Technical guidance availability is not proposal-specific acceptance.

name: Southern Water connection charging arrangements
fact: Southern Water states its 2026-27 new-connection charging arrangements took effect on 1 April 2026.
gate: Applicable charges do not establish capacity or engineering feasibility.

name: Severn Trent sewer adoption and pre-planning
fact: Severn Trent's adoption process uses pre-planning to confirm allowable discharge rates, identify capacity issues/diversions and then progresses to S104 design/adoption stages.
gate: Allowable discharge advice and adoption design are separate from planning permission and final connection rights.

name: Severn Trent developer applications and guidance
fact: Severn Trent separates development enquiry, new water main, sewer connection, Section 98, Section 104, diversion and pre-design processes.
gate: Application route selection does not prove technical approval or capacity.

name: South West Water developer charging arrangements
fact: South West Water publishes 2026-27 developer-services charging arrangements for new water and sewerage infrastructure supporting development and growth.
gate: Pricing rules are not site-specific capacity, design approval or planning permission.

name: South West Water public sewer connection application
fact: The current public-sewer connection application routes new sewer-connection enquiries through Developer Services and requires a specific work/site application process.
gate: An application form or work reference is not connection consent until approved.
